CHRONOLOGICAL FULL THREAD:

[1] 11 Aug 2026 13:11 UTC -- James Salas Guillen -> Kevin Lelitte, cc Simon Burford. Subject: "Cority - Applicant Data Import file".
Hi Kevin and Simon,

I wanted to provide an update on the Cority Applicant Data Import.

Following several uploads/imports in Production with real data, we've identified several formatting issues in the source report that require manual clean-up before the file can be successfully uploaded. These issues were not apparent during earlier testing and only became evident once we started processing production data.

The current report requires the following manual amendments before it can be uploaded to Cority:
1. Remove quotation marks from all fields (e.g. "First Name of Employee").
2. Ensure all column headers are contained within a single header row. Currently, the headers split across multiple rows when converted to CSV.
3. Format the Date of Birth field as a date only (dd/mm/yyyy) with no time component.
4. Ensure the file contains all 27 expected columns and corresponding headers even if no data is available.

Ideally, if the above changes can be implemented within the report itself, the report should be exported directly to CSV rather than Excel to eliminate the additional conversion and clean-up steps currently required.

As previously discussed, there may be an opportunity to implement these changes directly within the PXD reporting module, which would remove the need for ongoing manual work.

In addition, I have identified what appears to be a potential mismatch in the column mapping between our report and Cority. I currently have a support ticket open with the Cority support team to investigate this further. If the issue turns out to be on our side, we may also need to adjust the report column order accordingly.

Would it be possible to review whether these report changes can be made within PXD (RECSUP20_Applicant Cority Interface File)? Making these amendments at source would significantly reduce the manual effort required each time the file is processed for import.

Best wishes,
James Salas, Senior Functional Analyst, HR Systems | People Department | University of Oxford

[2] 18 Aug 2026 11:55 UTC -- Simon Burford replies (RE:).
Hi James,

I'm sure this is possible to do.

However, when I save the report as CSV and open it in notepad++ I see the following: [embedded screenshot -- see "Attachment note" below; the column headers to me look like they are in one row already, so how are you currently getting/viewing the CSV where it's split over multiple rows?]

Quotation marks in this file only exist where there is a comma in the data field, to prevent the columns breaking (e.g. in the screenshot above the division name "MATHS, PHYSICAL & LIFE SCIENCES" has a comma in it, so it adds quotes to stop the file interpreting MATHS as one column and PHYSICAL & LIFE SCIENCES as the next column). I'm assuming that this is expected behaviour and Cority can handle this?

The date of birth field is clearly an issue so this can hopefully be sorted, the headers are just the names of the text boxes but I have an idea of how this could be fixed so fingers crossed, but it definitely has commas denoting the columns even if the data is blank, so that should be fine.

Many thanks,
Simon Burford, HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager, HR Systems | People Department | University of Oxford

Thank you very much for looking into this. I have added my responses in red [inline in the quoted message -- reconstructed below since plain-text export flattens colour]:

- On "do headers need to retain spaces / exact labels": "The column headings do not need to retain the spaces and do not necessarily need to have the exact labels. - On "how was this report created / not on QA server / no change request": "This is a question for @Kevin, as I do not have direct access to this report. At the moment, I have been relying on a member of the FA team to export it for me."

Best wishes,
James Salas

I am starting to think that it might be worth exploring if we can set up an automated export of a CSV to a file location. Do you have a network folder that you would want CSV files to be saved to? I think by default it's exporting as the first option, i.e. absolutely no value, but I would want to explicitly set the fields to do this if we were to set up some automated process, just in case the global defaults change, so please confirm.
2 - Does Cority expect UTF-8 encoding? This looks like the default encoding for automated CSV exports so just need to check that this is ok for Cority?

Upon further investigation it looks like Lee might have created the report and perhaps it was still in testing when he left? Although it seems to be being used as a live interface file, so I'm really not sure. @Kevin Lelitte if you have anything to add from what Lee handed over when he left that would be helpful.

Simon Burford

prioritiesWeek.text: 38-day balance rollout — Work Group Holiday Scheme updates by department
prioritiesWeek.description:
New "38-day balance" leave/absence type rolling out via PeopleXD/WFM: departments move from their current holiday scheme (bank holidays and fixed closure dates pre-loaded) to a simple 38-day balance, where staff book bank holidays and closures themselves. Removes significant admin burden for new appointments and manual balance calculations. Roughly 9 holiday schemes currently in use across the university; policy hasn't been updated to match how the system calculates leave, so the annual leave dashboard exists as a workaround bridge — a policy change would be the proper fix but none is expected soon.

Department status (per the 19 Aug Granola meeting):
- Chemistry: keen to proceed, on WFM since October, a full year of admin pain. Main contact Jenna Boyce. Chemistry HR will pre-book bank holidays and fixed closure dates on staff's behalf this round.
- Maths: only on WFM since April, HR team still learning the system; recommendation is to advise them to pause and review after a full leave year rather than move now.
- GLAM: large department, many staff types, complex rosters/shift patterns (some staff on concentrated shifts, e.g. 4-day 9-hour, with managers currently recording leave at 7.23 hrs rather than actual shift length). Not all GLAM staff need moving — some are likely moving to rostering instead. GLAM has asked for a ballpark on how many work groups can be updated; no commitment given yet, pending Chemistry's confirmed workgroup count. GLAM offered to pay for the work; no charging mechanism exists yet so it's too late to charge this year — needs a proper process for future years.
- Biology: declining for this year — came in too late (likely heard about the approach via Anna's promotional sessions).

Mechanics: HR teams send a list of affected work groups (code + description); Kevin updates the Holiday Scheme attached to each work group, swapping to the scheme with no bank holidays/fixed closure dates. Nothing to create — pure data update. Michael estimated ~1-2 minutes per work group at a realistic pace. Kevin will personally do the Work Group updates once resourcing/timing is confirmed.

Timing: must align with annual leave rollover (7 October); work can begin 5 October once the previous year is locked. Deadline for departments to submit their work group lists is 28 August. Priority order is first department to submit data gets done first. Risk flagged: departments may try to change balances themselves without understanding the work-group link — staff won't be able to book bank holidays if their work group still has the old scheme attached, which will surface quickly as a support query; first-line support (Emma) needs briefing to handle this without escalating.

This is being treated as a pilot, not a standard service offering. GLAM's separate, larger rostering problem (Ashmolean/Botanic Gardens area) is not in scope here and is not currently resourced — see related tasks t035 and t2608181201061.

Julie is on leave from Fri 21 Aug to Wed 2 Sep 2026 (confirmed in the meeting — leave starts the day after the meeting); Marie Cooksey covers as department contact in her absence.
